description: Default capability for the main window. Filesystem access is the app's own data plus the folders the user picked (DEL-89, plans/fs-scope-plan.md). Static scope: $APPDATA/stores (the durable stores, M1) read-write, and $CONFIG/ohhi (the user resource root: layouts, keymaps, templates; ~/.config/ohhi on Linux) read-only through command scopes on exists, read-dir and read-text-file only. Nothing under $HOME. A vault folder enters the scope when the user picks it: the dialog plugin's open() with recursive: true grants it at runtime, tauri-plugin-persisted-scope saves the grant in Rust and restores it on the next launch, and src/lib.rs (granted_folders) mirrors each grant into a runtime capability so its dot-entries (.ohhi/, .obsidian/) match too (plugins.fs.requireLiteralLeadingDot is false in tauri.conf.json). Dropping a file or folder on the window grants it the same way (the fs plugin's own behaviour). The grant file, $APPDATA/.persisted-scope, is denied to the webview here as well as by the plugin, so a script in the webview cannot grant itself more on the next launch. Updater: check, download and install (not the download-and-install shortcut), plus process:allow-restart to relaunch into an installed update. The feed URL and signing key live in tauri.conf.json, so the webview can neither repoint the updater nor make it accept an unsigned build.
